players.comment: Grant won't return to Thursday's game against the Warriors due to a left calf injury. He'll finish with three points (1-2 FG, 1-1 3Pt) across five minutes. Grant limped to the locker room in the second quarter and was ruled out for the remainder of the contest shortly thereafter. If he's forced to miss additional time, Kris Murray and Olivier-Maxence Prosper would be candidates for increased minutes. Grant's next chance to play will come Saturday at Minnesota.

Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball. Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

Turner (shoulder) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Portland due to a left shoulder contusion, Turner will miss Thursday's contest after playing 21 minutes against Miami on Wednesday. His absence leaves Milwaukee without its primary rim protector and could create additional frontcourt opportunities for Bobby Portis and the team's reserves. Turner's next opportunity to return will come Saturday against Philadelphia, pending further injury updates

Kuzma (shoulder) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Portland due to a right shoulder contusion. Kuzma's absence further depletes Milwaukee's frontcourt, with Myles Turner (shoulder) also sidelined. Bobby Portis could see increased offensive opportunities, while additional minutes may become available to the team's reserve forwards. Kuzma's next opportunity to play comes Saturday against Philadelphia, depending on his recovery.

Ingram (heel/Achilles) will remain on the inactive list for Thursday's game in San Antonio. Ingram was cleared for full-contact work on Nov. 6, and he's been playing 5-on-5 for the past couple of weeks. Head coach Tyronn Lue said before Sunday's 113-105 win over the Hornets that he was hopeful Ingram would make his Clippers debut during their upcoming four-game road trip, so while he'll remain on the sidelines for Thursday's game, it sounds like there's a chance he could play Saturday in Dallas.

Brown (hamstring) went through individual work during Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. Brown is set to be re-evaluated this weekend due to a left hamstring strain, meaning his next chance to play will come Monday against Portland. Dean Wade (hamstring), Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Jabari Walker are all candidates for increased minutes while Brown is sidelined.

DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports. DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Warriors. The Grizzlies haven't shed very much light on the recovery of Jerome, who's missing a fourth straight contest. Cam Spencer remains a must-start fantasy option in nearly all fantasy leagues while Jerome is sidelined.

Williams (rest) is listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Bucks. Williams will take the night off Thursday after appearing in Portland's last five contests. He will presumably be back on the floor Saturday against the Knicks. In the meantime, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen should see more minutes behind Donovan Clingan.

Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports. Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic. It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

Williams (hamstring) has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated Saturday. Williams sustained a left hamstring strain in the Nov. 9 win over New Orleans, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against Boston. LJ Cryer will likely continue seeing increased burn in Williams' stead.

players.comment: Maxey (foot) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. Maxey was held out of Wednesday's win over Orlando due to right foot soreness, though he's trending in the right direction ahead of Saturday's game against Milwaukee. The Sixers should provide an update on the star point guard's status by Friday night, and if he's cleared to return, Anfernee Simons and Labaron Philon would likely see fewer minutes.

players.comment: Gardner (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the Bucks. Gardner was already in line to hit the bench in Pelle Larsson's (illness) return. He'll have some extra time to recover ahead of Sunday's showdown with the Thunder.

Pippen (back) is progressing in his recovery but is still considered week-to-week. Pippen hasn't played since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a firm timetable to return.  Cam Spencer and Javon Small will likely continue seeing increased playing time in Pippen's absence.

players.comment: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced. Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

Edey (hip) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Warriors. Edey is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back. If healthy, Isaiah Stewart (illness) would draw the spot start at center in all likelihood.

Avdija (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game against the Bucks. A foot injury continues to bother Avdija, who will now miss his second consecutive contest. His next opportunity to get back on the court will come Saturday versus the Knicks. In the meantime, Sidy Cissoko is expected to remain in the starting lineup.

players.comment: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bucks. Youngblood has been sidelined since Nov. 10 due to a right foot injury, with his latest designation identifying the heel as the affected area. The rookie guard had shown flashes of perimeter shooting before the injury, connecting on multiple three-pointers in three consecutive appearances. His next opportunity to return will come Saturday against the Knicks, though his limited role leaves him off the fantasy radar in most formats.

Barlow (back) is trending toward making his season debut in Saturday's game against the Bucks, Tony Jones of The Athletic reports. Barlow is nearing his season debut after missing an extended period with a back injury. The Sixers should provide an update on the 23-year-old big man's status by Friday night. According to Chris Hine of The Philly Inquirer, Barlow was a full participant at Friday's practice.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN. It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports. Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.

players.comment: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports. The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months. Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

Bona (back) participated in Friday's practice, though he still needs to go through a full practice with contact before being cleared to return to game action, Adam Aaronson of PhillyVoice.com reports. Bona hasn't played since Nov. 4 due to a back sprain, though he appears to be trending in the right direction. Until the big man is cleared to play, Dominick Barlow (back) and Jabari Walker are candidates for increased minutes.

Lawal is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors due to tightness in his right groin. It sounds like the rookie forward is dealing with a minor issue. His next chance to suit up comes Saturday against the Clippers.

Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

players.comment: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio. Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports. Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

Green (elbow) is out for Thursday's game against the Grizzlies. Nick Friedell of The Athletic reported Wednesday that the veteran forward would sit out the second half of this back-to-back set, and now it's official. Al Horford should help pick up the slack for the Warriors on Thursday.
